read: PSO's headline P/E of 3.74 looks cheap and the composite model puts fair value at 402.19 (+16.5% vs. price), but that composite masks a huge spread across methods — earnings-power/relative-PE methods say 500-590, DDM says just 57 — so the 'cheap' verdict leans on non-dividend approaches for a business that pays out only 10.6% of earnings. Forward P/E (4.73) sitting above trailing P/E (3.74) signals the market expects EPS to soften, which cuts against a simple 'cheap and safe' story. Net margin is thin (~1.4%), typical for an oil marketing volume/margin business with no debt or receivables data in this feed to check circular-debt exposure. The dividend itself is low-payout and well-covered by current earnings, just not generous.
earnings_quality: Thin net margin (~1.4%, net income 43.53B on 3.21T revenue); forward P/E (4.73) above trailing P/E (3.74) implies the market is pricing in an EPS decline, not growth.
dividend_safety: Payout ratio only 10.60% against Rs92.73 EPS — recent dividend (Rs10/share, ~2.9% yield, closure 2025-10-17) looks well-covered but the yield itself is modest, not an income play.
balance_sheet_flags: receivables/circular-debt exposure (typical OMC risk) not in the data
beta 0.45 (low relative volatility, not a leverage signal)

claim.text: PSO's next reported results (due on/around Aug 21, 2026) will show net margin still in the thin ~1-1.5% band, not a step-change improvement, tempering the composite-model's 16.5% undervaluation case.
